races.name: Visit attheraces.com EBF Fillies' Novice Stakes (GBB Race) (IRE Incentive Race)

runners_data.name: Etonnante
runners_data.spotlight: This second foal of a Listed-placed 1m AW winner is a half-sister to French Group-placed 1m AW winner Eponine (including 2yo; RPR 101); the outside stall isn't ideal for a newcomer but she makes obvious paper appeal for her very powerful yard.

runners_data.name: Aura Of Melania
runners_data.spotlight: Cost 12,000gns at the breeze-ups and is out of a mare who was runner-up from 1m-1m4f (including 2yo; RPR 78); the Roger Fell stable is going well but isn't a regular source of first-time-out 2yo success.

runners_data.name: Sovereign Beach
runners_data.spotlight: 62,000gns breeze-up buy who is a half-sister to four winners, notably So Majestic (Listed-placed 5f; RPR 97); stable has yet to hit the target with 2yos in 2026 but has enjoyed plenty of first-time-out juvenile success in recent years; would very much enter the reckoning if the betting vibes are strong.

runners_data.name: Lady Branksome
runners_data.spotlight: Sent off favourite for last week's 6f Kempton debut but was trapped wider than ideal from an outside draw and faded inside the final furlong; has the rail draw this time; likely improver.

runners_data.name: Fern Clyde
runners_data.spotlight: Stepped up on her debut when just under 2l fourth of eight over C&D (good) 12 days ago; that form is below the level it usually requires to win a race like this so she'll almost certainly need to improve again.

runners_data.name: Bladey Lady
runners_data.spotlight: Minzaal half-sister to six winners but didn't achieve much when beaten just under 8l into third on her 5f Beverley debut (good to firm) 16 days ago; may do better but Fern Clyde is the more obvious of the Tim Easterby pair.

runners_data.name: Suzie May
runners_data.spotlight: Poor form in two outings at Beverley, finishing behind the reopposing Bladey Lady when a remote fourth latterly.

races.name: Book Now At ripon-races.co.uk Handicap

runners_data.name: Harswell River
runners_data.note: Natural leader from ideal draw but exposed after 19 starts, relies on controlling tempo from the front
runners_data.spotlight: Exposed, having raced 19 times, but has placed three times at up to 1m at Redcar (good/good to firm) this spring; handily drawn for one who tends to race close to the pace; should go well for in-form Roger Fell.

runners_data.name: Vega's Virtue
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse stepping up in trip for first time, needs strong pace to close into
runners_data.spotlight: No significant impact in handicaps over 7f at Doncaster and 6f here this spring; still fairly early days but needs a combination of a step up in trip and first-time cheekpieces to make a difference.

runners_data.name: Wondrous
runners_data.note: Prominent runner returning after 238-day break, potential improver over longer trip
runners_data.spotlight: Beat only a couple home in three qualifying runs over 6f last year but rates a potential improver now handicapping over a longer trip on her return; market support would look significant.

runners_data.name: That's Enough
runners_data.note: Unknown style switching from AW to turf, fading tendency limits appeal over 1m
runners_data.spotlight: Raced on AW; 66-1 when well held on 7f Kempton handicap debut four weeks ago; still early days but a switch to turf needs to spark improvement.

runners_data.name: Crystal Aurora
runners_data.note: Hold-up type needing revival after 131-day break, ordinary AW winter form
runners_data.spotlight: Seven-race maiden; third on 6f Pontefract handicap debut (soft) last autumn but well held in two AW outings over the winter; revival needed after a break.

runners_data.name: Hood Wink
runners_data.note: Recent winner who can track pace, failed to follow up twice since Wetherby success
runners_data.spotlight: Dead-heated at Wetherby (1m, good to firm) in April but has failed to back that up twice since (including C&D).

runners_data.name: Contemplation
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse struggling since yard switch, no threat in three runs for new connections
runners_data.spotlight: 0-4 for James Ferguson and hasn't threatened in three runs for new yard.

runners_data.name: Captain Bruce
runners_data.note: Hold-up type with serious form decline, tailed off in all three starts this year
runners_data.spotlight: Won 7f/1m2f AW handicaps for Nigel Tinkler last year but has finished tailed off on all three starts this term, including back on turf for new yard 16 days ago.

runners_data.name: Eva The Deeva
runners_data.note: Hold-up mare stepping up to handicaps, Tinkler yard in good form recently
runners_data.spotlight: Never dangerous in three outings over 6f/7f this spring but stands a much more realistic chance now handicapping and the Nigel Tinkler team has really hit form; improvement would come as no surprise.

runners_data.name: Regal Knight
runners_data.note: Natural leader likely to pressure Harswell River early, trip reduction may help
runners_data.spotlight: No significant impact in a pair of 1m2f handicaps this year, hanging under pressure at Beverley last time; a drop back in trip needs to help him find more.

races.paceDynamic: Harswell River and Regal Knight will both break alertly and contest the early lead, with Harswell River's natural pace-forcing style likely to dictate from stall 1. Wondrous may also show early speed from a wide draw before settling, creating a solid gallop that should stretch the field entering the home straight. The honest pace will expose the stamina limitations of several hold-up horses who fade in the finish, while favoring prominent racers who can track the leaders without getting into an early speed duel. This race shape strongly favors prominent runners who can position close to the pace and kick clear when the early leaders weaken.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Prominent tracker prevails
scenarios.trigger: If Wondrous or Hood Wink can sit second or third behind the dueling leaders
scenarios.body: The honest gallop will set up perfectly for a horse that can travel strongly in behind and strike when Harswell River and Regal Knight tire in the final furlong. Hood Wink's recent Wetherby win shows he can capitalize on this tactical scenario.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front runner dominates
scenarios.trigger: If Harswell River breaks cleanly and gets an easy lead without serious pressure
scenarios.body: His natural pace advantage and good draw will allow him to control the tempo and kick clear when the field comes to challenge, making his exposed form less relevant. The lack of sustained early pressure plays directly into his strengths.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late closer strikes
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace becomes too strong between Harswell River and Regal Knight
scenarios.body: The speed duel will collapse in the final quarter-mile, setting up a finish for hold-up horses who can produce their best late kick. Crystal Aurora or Vega's Virtue could benefit from the pace scenario despite their ordinary recent form.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Improver emerges
scenarios.trigger: If Wondrous shows the expected improvement from her long break and step up in trip
scenarios.body: Her early pace will position her perfectly to strike when the leaders tire, and the 238-day break could have freshened her significantly. Market support would confirm trainer confidence in her chances.

watchPoints.text: Harswell River breaks slowly from stall 1 and loses his natural pace advantage
Strong market support for Wondrous would signal significant improvement expected from break
Hood Wink travels strongly in behind the leaders through the first half-mile
Regal Knight and Harswell River engage in sustained speed duel from flag-fall
Vega's Virtue gets cover and switches off properly for first attempt over 1m

races.name: Sky Sports Racing Sky 415 Handicap

runners_data.name: Black Missile
runners_data.note: Prominent runner suited by moderate pace, solid recent form suggests ready for competitive handicap debut
runners_data.spotlight: Made the frame on all three 2yo starts (5f-6f) and again showed clear promise when fifth of 14 on recent seasonal/handicap debut at Beverley (5f, good to soft), despite racing too freely in the early stages and hanging left at the business end; back up in trip and 2lb lower here; a possible.

runners_data.name: North West Gal
runners_data.note: Proven prominent style ideal for tactical affair, Quinn stable in good form recently
runners_data.spotlight: Ended four-race 2yo season with 5f AW novice win in November and made encouraging reappearance when fifth in Catterick handicap (6f, good; short of room towards finish) this month; contender if that recent outing brought her on.

runners_data.name: Valor Spirit
runners_data.note: Hold-up style disadvantaged by likely slow pace, long absence adds uncertainty despite previous promise
runners_data.spotlight: 0-8 as a 2yo for Richard Fahey, albeit having made the frame six times; changed hands for 20,000gns in the autumn and was subsequently gelding; reappears on a workable mark; market may guide.

runners_data.name: Country Artiste
runners_data.note: Confirmed leader will dictate fractions uncontested, poor recent form but tactical advantage significant
runners_data.spotlight: Started off for Craig Lidster with two very underwhelming AW runs in January (6f/5f) and is now 0-9 overall; difficult to enthuse over on first start for four months.

runners_data.name: Simba's Pride
runners_data.note: Form horse with prominent style perfectly suited, recent C&D second suggests more to come
runners_data.spotlight: Suited by drop back in trip when scoring on this month's handicap debut at Hamilton (6f, good) and probably bettered that performance when close second over C&D (good) a fortnight later; back in action before 1lb nudge takes effect and nicely drawn towards nearside rail; big player.

runners_data.name: Uncertainty
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner faces difficult task in slowly-run race, stable switch hasn't clicked yet
runners_data.spotlight: Second in 7f AW nursery on final run for Richard Hannon but well beaten on both starts for new stable, latterly in 6f Doncaster handicap on seasonal reappearance 12 days ago; others have much less to prove.

runners_data.name: Head For Freedom
runners_data.note: Encouraging C&D fourth last time but hold-up style works against likely race shape
runners_data.spotlight: Made encouraging seasonal debut when fourth of 13 over C&D (good to soft) last month and had some excuses when below that form over 5f at Beverley 24 days ago (suffered interference in first half of race); on a good mark now and enters calculations.

runners_data.name: Come On Over
runners_data.note: Prominent runner but poor recent form and maiden status concern against this field
runners_data.spotlight: Eight-race maiden who was safely held over 5f on first two starts for new stable this spring, albeit having encountered traffic on first occasion; ought to be suited by this move back up in trip, though, and may yet come good for David O'Meara.

runners_data.name: Northern Tempest
runners_data.note: Free-running style could work against him if racing keenly, stable has better chance with Simba's Pride
runners_data.spotlight: Soundly beaten after racing too freely in two AW handicaps (6f/7f) this spring and has now been unplaced all five starts; stable has a much more obvious chance with Simba's Pride.

runners_data.name: Great Success
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner disadvantaged by race shape, tendency to race freely adds complications
runners_data.spotlight: Still unexposed after only four runs but was beaten about 19l after racing too freely on last month's seasonal/handicap debut (7f) and is drawn on the wing for this sprint return.

runners_data.name: Solar Cooper
runners_data.note: Recent C&D winner in cheekpieces but hold-up style faces tactical disadvantage here
runners_data.spotlight: Started off for new stable with two down-the-field runs last month but bounced back to form with clear C&D (good) win in first-time cheekpices 11 days ago; not ideally drawn today and goes without cheekpieces this time but still respected under 6lb penalty (due to go up that amount anyway).

races.paceDynamic: Country Artiste will lead unchallenged with Black Missile, North West Gal, Simba's Pride and Come On Over settling prominently behind. The lack of natural pace pressure means Country Artiste can dictate fractions and potentially steal a march on the field. This creates a tactical race where the prominent runners can track the moderate gallop and kick clear, while hold-up horses like Valor Spirit, Uncertainty and Head For Freedom face a difficult task making up ground in a slowly-run affair. The race shape strongly favours prominent/tracking runners who can position close to the pace without pressure.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Uncontested Leader Steals
scenarios.trigger: If Country Artiste is allowed to bowl along in front without serious pressure through halfway
scenarios.body: The modest gallop suits his stamina and he can quicken clear when the field comes under pressure. Prominent runners tracking him are best placed to respond if he falters.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Runners Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If the pace-tracking horses can stalk Country Artiste comfortably and produce late kicks
scenarios.body: Simba's Pride and North West Gal are proven over the trip with tactical speed to exploit the moderate gallop. They can position perfectly and strike decisively in the final furlong.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Surge
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is genuinely slow and hold-up horses get splits in the straight
scenarios.body: Valor Spirit and Head For Freedom can unleash finishing kicks from off the pace. The lack of early pace allows them to close strongly despite their preferred style working against them.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Scramble
scenarios.trigger: If Country Artiste stops quickly and multiple runners converge in a bunched finish
scenarios.body: The moderate early gallop leaves many horses with chances turning for home creating a cavalry charge. Fitness and finishing kick become paramount in a messy conclusion.

watchPoints.text: Country Artiste's early fractions - if allowed to amble in front he becomes very dangerous despite poor form
Northern Tempest pulling hard early - his tendency to race keenly could compromise his finishing kick
Simba's Pride's position turning for home - perfectly placed to strike if tracking the leader successfully
Any hold-up horse trapped behind Country Artiste if he sets modest fractions and kicks clear late
Solar Cooper settles in cheekpieces - needs to overcome tactical disadvantage of hold-up style in slow race

races.name: Ripon Cathedral Handicap

runners_data.name: El Matador
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner with strong recent form who should get clear run from the back but needs to prove stamina for this trip
runners_data.spotlight: Low-mileage 4yo who has been a good second at Lingfield (7f, AW) and Redcar (1m, good) this spring; hasn't necessarily shaped as if crying out for this trip but he's likely to be bang there again if his stamina holds.

runners_data.name: Londoner
runners_data.note: Prominent runner facing traffic concerns but proven at this distance with solid form including course win
runners_data.spotlight: Usually thereabouts, including in AW campaign this year which culminated in a Lingfield 1m2f win in April; respectable fifth of nine off this mark at Chester (extended 1m2f, good) three weeks ago.

runners_data.name: Parole d'Oro
runners_data.note: Hold-up type returning from 13-day break who could benefit if pace collapses but needs to bounce back from poor last run
runners_data.spotlight: Sole success came at Epsom (7f, good to firm) as a 2yo, though he twice finished runner-up last year, including at York (1m2f, good; first start since being gelded) in October; didn't enjoy the smoothest run and far from disgraced in good Newbury handicap on reappearance; likely to go well.

runners_data.name: James McHenry
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with course form but 28 days since last run may blunt his sharpness in crowded early positions
runners_data.spotlight: Course winner who was runner-up in the 2024 Cambridgeshire but has been lightly raced since; his keeping-on fifth of 12 over 1m1f at Musselburgh in April suggests most of that ability remains but he failed to build on it tackling 1m2f for the first time when fourth at Redcar (good to firm) four weeks ago; first-time cheekpieces worn at Redcar are retained.

runners_data.name: Garden Oasis
runners_data.note: Natural leader with seven course wins getting significant weight relief but age concerns at 11 years old
runners_data.spotlight: Front-running 11yo with seven course wins, the latest gained over 1m (good) last spring; creditable placed efforts on his last three starts (including C&D) and should give it another good shot, for all this is a higher grade than he's been contesting.

runners_data.name: Prince Of The Seas
runners_data.note: Prominent runner switching to 5lb claimer but form has declined since yard move and faces traffic issues
runners_data.spotlight: Narrow win at Goodwood (1m4f, good to firm) for Ralph Beckett last summer; not disgraced on 1m4f course reappearance for new yard but went backwards from that at the York Dante meeting since; the first-time cheekpieces he wore there are quickly discarded; also down in trip.

runners_data.name: Spioradalta
runners_data.note: Recent course winner over this trip who races prominently but must overcome traffic from Chester flop
runners_data.spotlight: Enhanced his good Ripon record with a narrow win over this trip on good to soft last month; faded to finish well held at Chester since (Londoner ahead of him) but a revival can't be ruled out back here.

runners_data.name: Austrian Theory
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner on career-low mark but regressive form trend suggests he needs significant improvement
runners_data.spotlight: On a losing run and went backwards from C&D reappearance fifth to Spioradalta when well held at Hamilton a fortnight ago; on a career-low mark but need to see more.

runners_data.name: Financer
runners_data.note: Patient type who could benefit from pace setup but needs to prove he can recapture form from 13 days ago
runners_data.spotlight: Runner-up three times last season, including C&D; respectable fourth of ten to Spioradalta on C&D reappearance (good to soft); well beaten at the York Dante meeting since but should find this a bit easier.

runners_data.name: Spirit Of Acklam
runners_data.note: Prominent runner returning after 362-day absence which raises serious fitness concerns despite past course success
runners_data.spotlight: Scored with a fair degree of authority at Ayr (1m2f, good; from 2lb lower) in April 2025; absent since toiling at Chester 362 days ago, which raises concerns, but he did win over C&D on his 2024 reappearance; the betting should help to guide expectations.

races.paceDynamic: Garden Oasis will lead uncontested, setting a genuine gallop that suits his front-running style over this 1m2f trip. Four prominent runners (Londoner, James McHenry, Prince Of The Seas, Spioradalta) will create congestion tracking the leader, but none will pressure the pace early. The hold-up horses (El Matador, Parole d'Oro, Austrian Theory, Financer) will need to navigate traffic in the straight as those prominent runners fan out. This race shape strongly favours the leader Garden Oasis and patient hold-up types who can find clear runs, while the prominent pack face tactical disadvantage from overcrowding.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Garden Oasis Wires Field
scenarios.trigger: If Garden Oasis maintains his lead turning for home without being challenged
scenarios.body: The 11-year-old course specialist exploits his uncontested advantage and his 13lb weight allowance proves decisive. The prominent quartet get in each other's way when trying to mount challenges, allowing the leader to hold on gamely.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent runners create a pace collapse by going too slow early
scenarios.body: Patient types like El Matador and Parole d'Oro get perfect setups from the back, finding clear runs while the early pace-trackers have nothing left. The superior class of these hold-up horses tells in a sprint finish.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Runner Breaks Clear
scenarios.trigger: If one of Londoner, Spioradalta or James McHenry detaches from the pack
scenarios.body: The winner breaks the prominent logjam by going early enough to avoid traffic but late enough to catch a tiring Garden Oasis. Superior tactical positioning from an experienced jockey makes the difference.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos Benefits Outsider
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses completely and multiple horses get badly hampered
scenarios.body: The race becomes a messy scramble where an unfancied runner like Spirit Of Acklam or Austrian Theory finds the clearest passage. Class goes out the window in favour of luck and positioning.

watchPoints.text: Garden Oasis breaking clear early could steal an unassailable lead if the prominent quartet go too conservatively
Traffic problems developing at the 2f pole when Londoner, James McHenry, Prince Of The Seas and Spioradalta all need racing room simultaneously
El Matador and Parole d'Oro tracking too close to the pace early would compromise their preferred hold-up tactics
Spirit Of Acklam showing any signs of a hard race given his 362-day layoff and fitness questions
Austrian Theory and Financer getting squeezed for room if the hold-up contingent gets bunched turning for home

races.name: Sky Sports Racing Virgin 519 Handicap

runners_data.name: Tickets
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer who needs strong pace to be effective, 21 days off may leave him needing the run despite eye-catching Southwell effort
runners_data.spotlight: Short of room before catching the eye with late headway for fifth over 7f at Southwell three weeks ago; has done most of his winning on AW but a fast-ground win at Redcar last spring shows he's effective on turf; Jet Warrior has to be considered the stable number one but he's still of interest.

runners_data.name: Tarlac
runners_data.note: Likely lone leader but poor recent form suggests he may not have the class to capitalize even with tactical advantage
runners_data.spotlight: Sole win from 19 starts came over C&D last May but he's falling in the weights without giving any obvious indication he's likely to take advantage; a first-time visor replaces the blinkers worn last time.

runners_data.name: Night Emperor
runners_data.note: Hold-up type who showed improvement switching to Tina Jackson, the 21-day break freshens him up for this easier grade
runners_data.spotlight: Failed to progress for Hugo Palmer; fared a lot better than on his AW stable debut in February when sixth (Hurstwood fourth) of 12 at Redcar (6f, good) three weeks ago but will need to step forward again.

runners_data.name: Hurstwood
runners_data.note: Past winner here with prominent style, fourth at Redcar suggests he's sharpening up nicely for this target
runners_data.spotlight: Won this race in 2023 and 2025; sharper for his reappearance when respectable fourth of 12 at Redcar (6f, good) three weeks ago and may come on again; a must for the shortlist.

runners_data.name: Jet Warrior
runners_data.note: Last week's easy Ayr winner has the class edge and proven finishing kick, 5lb penalty still leaves him well-handicapped
runners_data.spotlight: Came good with an easy 6f win at Ayr (good to firm) under Clifford Lee last week; 5lb well in under a penalty compared to his future mark so his claims are obvious.

runners_data.name: Golden Prosperity
runners_data.note: Non-runner
runners_data.comment: Won over 5f at Catterick in April but subsequent defeats underline his inconsistency
runners_data.spotlight: Successful off this mark at Catterick (5f, good) in April but four lesser runs have followed, including at Redcar on Tuesday.

runners_data.name: Barmyblade
runners_data.note: Out of form but dual C&D winner last season, needs to bounce back from poor Nottingham run just 9 days ago
runners_data.spotlight: Arrives out of sorts (well beaten at Nottingham just nine days ago) but a revival can't be completely ruled out given he won twice over C&D (good) last May.

runners_data.name: Solar Biricz
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse whose visor worked well at Redcar in April, disappointing Thirsk effort suggests headgear impact is inconsistent
runners_data.spotlight: Better signs for new stable when fourth at Redcar (5f, good to firm) in a first-time visor in April but the headgear didn't work anywhere near as well at Thirsk 12 days ago and is left off now.

runners_data.name: Angel Of England
runners_data.note: Prominent early but fades badly, poor recent form and questionable stamina make her vulnerable in any scenario
runners_data.spotlight: Went desperately close at Newcastle (6f) in December but has struggled for form since.

runners_data.name: Ridgemaster
runners_data.note: 66-1 Newcastle winner but three heavy defeats since suggest that was a fluke, hold-up style suits but lacks class
runners_data.spotlight: Caused a 66-1 shock when winning a 7f handicap at Newcastle on his stable debut in December but three heavy defeats have followed, including dropped to 6f back on turf last time.

races.paceDynamic: Tarlac will likely lead uncontested from the start, having shown prominent tendencies and possessing the only confirmed front-running profile in this field. With most runners preferring to settle behind (Tickets, Night Emperor, Jet Warrior, Solar Biricz, Ridgemaster all hold-up types), and only Hurstwood, Barmyblade potentially racing prominently early, Tarlac should get an easy time in front. The lack of pace pressure will create a tactical race with a sprint finish developing from the 2f pole. This shape strongly favors hold-up horses who can produce late kicks, particularly those with proven finishing speed over this trip.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If Tarlac sets uncontested fractions and the pace stays steady through halfway
scenarios.body: The lack of early pace allows closers to conserve energy and time their challenges perfectly in the final 2f. Jet Warrior's recent Ayr win shows he has the class edge when getting the right setup, while Tickets thrives when able to unleash late speed.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Duo Press Leader
scenarios.trigger: If Hurstwood and Barmyblade decide to take the race on early and press Tarlac for the lead
scenarios.body: The increased pace stretches out the field and creates opportunities for horses just off the pace to strike. Barmyblade's C&D wins last season show he can handle aggressive tactics here, while the strong gallop suits Hurstwood's proven staying power.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Tarlac Gets Away
scenarios.trigger: If the pace stays extremely slow with no challengers willing to commit until very late
scenarios.body: Tarlac steals a march turning for home and holds off late challengers who leave their runs too late. His C&D win last May proves he can capitalize when getting ideal conditions, while the 134lbs weight keeps him competitive.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses Completely
scenarios.trigger: If all runners sit and wait creating a crawling pace through 4f
scenarios.body: The race becomes a pure sprint from the 2f marker favoring the most naturally speedy finishers. Solar Biricz's visor addition could spark improvement in a dash, while any horse with tactical speed gains a decisive edge.

watchPoints.text: Jet Warrior could win decisively if getting the expected soft lead setup, having shown superior class at Ayr last week
Tarlac may get uncontested lead but watch for any early pressure from Hurstwood or Barmyblade that could compromise his stamina
Angel Of England and Ridgemaster both show concerning fade patterns that make them poor value even in tactical scenarios
Tickets could be the value play if the pace develops strongly enough to suit his proven late kick
Watch the market for Hurstwood given his course record and the potential for connections to have him primed for another win here

races.name: Napoleons Casino And Restaurant Leeds Handicap

runners_data.name: Spartan Times
runners_data.note: Natural leader returning from 217-day break via hurdles win but has proven 1m4f course form on similar going
runners_data.spotlight: Notched four Flat wins last year, including over 1m3f here on good; returned from a break to win over hurdles at Uttoxeter (2m, good) this month; only a fair fourth at Aintree since but still respected back on the Flat.

runners_data.name: Sir Edward Lear
runners_data.note: Prominent racer who may have needed his reappearance 13 days ago and is back to a winning mark
runners_data.spotlight: This course scorer might have needed his recent reappearance and is well treated if bouncing back to his best, having returned to the mark he defied at Newmarket (1m2f, good to firm) last August; also went close over C&D last summer; cheekpieces off, visor back on; yard hasn't been as prolific as usual in the last couple of weeks but that's likely to change before long.

runners_data.name: Polygram
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse switching trainers who will struggle with the likely honest early pace in a small field
runners_data.spotlight: Went close more than once for Harry Charlton but left that yard an eight-race maiden; hasn't threatened to put that right in four runs for new stable but went with a bit more promise when sixth of 11 over 1m3f at Hamilton 11 days ago, keeping on from off the pace after missing the break again; due to be 2lb lower from the weekend.

runners_data.name: Something
runners_data.note: Front runner who won this race last year off higher mark but has been out of form in six recent starts
runners_data.spotlight: Made all in this race off 2lb higher on good to soft for Jedd O'Keeffe last year; drew a blank in six outings for Stuart Williams but latest 1m4f Doncaster third on good to firm was respectable; sold for 8,000gns since; could make another bold bid in this race.

runners_data.name: So Alex
runners_data.note: Prominent runner returning from 159-day absence with Tapeta form that may not translate to turf
runners_data.spotlight: Progressed in his first three handicaps, winning over 1m4f on Wolverhampton's Tapeta in November/December; something can't have been right when well held there just before Christmas; absent subsequently and makes first turf start since his debut; remains with potential.

races.paceDynamic: Spartan Times and Something both show clear leading tendencies and will contest the early pace in this small field. With only five runners over 1m4f, the early gallop should be honest but not frantic as both front runners have stamina for the trip. The lack of genuine hold-up horses means the pace won't collapse, creating a searching test that will expose any fitness doubts. This race shape strongly favours horses with early pace and tactical speed who can position prominently from the start.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Front Runner Dominates
scenarios.trigger: If Spartan Times or Something establishes a clear early lead without serious pressure
scenarios.body: The leader gets into a rhythm and has enough left to repel late challenges on the testing climb to Ripon's finish. Early positioning proves crucial with limited time to make up ground in a small, strung-out field.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Duel Backfires
scenarios.trigger: If Spartan Times and Something engage in a prolonged speed battle through the early stages
scenarios.body: Both leaders weaken in the final two furlongs after their exertions, allowing the prominent racers to sweep past with superior finishing kicks. Sir Edward Lear's class and So Alex's fresh legs become decisive factors.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Tactical Speed Wins
scenarios.trigger: If one of the prominent runners positions perfectly behind the early pace without getting involved
scenarios.body: They inherit a perfect stalking position as the leaders soften each other up, then strike decisively in the straight. The winner gets the best of both worlds - cover early and a clear run when it matters.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Staying Power Emerges
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace collapses and the race becomes a test of pure stamina
scenarios.body: The lack of genuine speed creates a slow-motion finish where proven stayers can grind out victory despite unfavorable positioning. Distance specialists thrive in the attritional conditions.

watchPoints.text: Spartan Times may need this first run back on the flat after a 7-month absence despite his recent hurdles success
Something's front-running style could lead to a pace duel with Spartan Times that suits the prominent runners behind
Sir Edward Lear's fitness after his recent reappearance could be the key to his chances of improving significantly
Polygram's hold-up style is poorly suited to a small field with two confirmed leaders setting honest early fractions
So Alex faces a significant test returning to turf after his recent Tapeta successes at Wolverhampton

runners_data.name: South Parade
runners_data.note: Uncontested leader but poor recent form suggests she cannot sustain her gallop when challenged late
runners_data.spotlight: On a dangerous mark but she doesn't look in much form, finishing down the field again at Thirsk (Tees Aggregates several places ahead of her) 12 days ago; needs to rediscover her spark.

runners_data.name: Our Absent Friends
runners_data.note: Prominent runner returning from 60-day break with proven course form but question marks over current sharpness
runners_data.spotlight: Seven wins, the latest at Newcastle in December off a 6lb lower mark; good second off 1lb lower back at Newcastle in March but well held back on turf at Doncaster later that month; freshened up since.

runners_data.name: Tees Aggregates
runners_data.note: Strong closer with excellent recent course form, though Jack Nicholls' 5lb claim partially offsets difficult rides
runners_data.spotlight: Doesn't always look the easiest of rides but recent efforts respectable (fifth of 17 at Thirsk latest) and he's been successful on the last two occasions he's dropped into a 0-70; considered.

runners_data.name: Dc Cogent
runners_data.note: Consistent hold-up horse seeking first handicap win but proven ability to hit the frame repeatedly
runners_data.spotlight: AW maiden winner; 0-14 in handicaps but is in a consistent vein of form, reaching the frame three times this spring, including third to Herakles at Nottingham (5f, good); met trouble when a beaten favourite at Carlisle last week and can have that effort ignored.

runners_data.name: Herakles
runners_data.note: Course winner with momentum from Nottingham victory, perfectly suited to come from off the pace
runners_data.spotlight: C&D winner; consistent in defeat on AW before making a successful return to turf at Nottingham (5f, good) 19 days ago, with reopposing Dc Cogent and Marajito behind in third and fifth; did that quite comfortably but a 6lb rise puts him 3lb above his highest win mark of 66; has also yet to score back-to-back in his 41-race career.

runners_data.name: Canaria Queen
runners_data.note: In-form prominent runner carrying 5lb penalty but Tim Easterby stable in excellent form with 9/103 strike rate
runners_data.spotlight: Made it two wins in last three starts when seeing off seven rivals at Musselburgh (5f, good) last Thursday; a 5lb penalty shouldn't prevent another bold bid in her current mood.

runners_data.name: Marajito
runners_data.note: Front-rank horse reconnecting with form, held up better by pace scenario than early prominence suggests
runners_data.spotlight: Made all in maiden handicap at Redcar (5f, good to firm) last June; disappointing after that in 2025 but more encouraging signs when fifth of nine to Herakles (Dc Cogent third) on Nottingham reappearance 19 days ago, fading late as if the outing was just needed; enters calculations having dipped 2lb below her winning mark.

runners_data.name: Wrestling Revenue
runners_data.note: Light-weighted hold-up horse returning from poor recent course effort but proven 5f handicap winner
runners_data.spotlight: Well backed when winning a 5f handicap at Pontefract (soft) last October but hasn't matched that since, including beating only one home over C&D three weeks ago; back on the mark he defied at Pontefract but would need to see money for him again.

races.paceDynamic: South Parade will make the pace unopposed with Our Absent Friends, Canaria Queen and Marajito content to track just behind rather than challenge early. The lack of genuine pace pressure means the leaders can dictate reasonable fractions over this minimum trip. Tees Aggregates, Dc Cogent, Herakles and Wrestling Revenue will be held up seeking cover before unleashing late runs. This sustainable pace scenario clearly favors the prominent and hold-up horses who can quicken late, as South Parade's recent poor form suggests she cannot sustain her gallop when challenged.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Sustainable Pace Suits Closers
scenarios.trigger: If South Parade sets reasonable fractions without early pressure...
scenarios.body: The hold-up horses get the perfect setup to unleash telling late runs in the final furlong. Tees Aggregates and Herakles can use their proven finishing kicks to maximum effect.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Trackers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace becomes genuinely slow...
scenarios.body: Canaria Queen and Our Absent Friends can kick clear from their tracking positions before the hold-up horses can respond. Their race fitness and tactical positioning proves decisive.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front Runner Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If South Parade finds improved form and the pace becomes truly testing...
scenarios.body: She can exploit her uncontested lead to build an unassailable advantage. The closers find insufficient time to make up the deficit despite their superior finishing speed.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Scramble
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace becomes crawling and no one wants to lead...
scenarios.body: The race becomes a sprint from the furlong pole where pure speed matters most. Wrestling Revenue's light weight becomes crucial in a bunched finish.

watchPoints.text: South Parade could steal this if she shows any spark of her old ability given her uncontested lead
Canaria Queen's penalty and quick reappearance after Thursday's Musselburgh win may take its toll late
Tees Aggregates needs Jack Nicholls to settle him properly early given his reputation for difficult rides
Our Absent Friends' 60-day absence could be significant positive or negative given his inconsistent nature
Wrestling Revenue's light weight of 122lbs makes him dangerous if the pace sets up perfectly for closers
